title: red-first names the task's own case by its label, and reads only the runner that ran
desiredOutcome: stamp-verification red recognises a house case whose label starts with an ordinary word as the task's own, and an expected ERROR: line from a passing house case is no longer counted as a failing unittest case, so a genuine red-first reads proved.

A literal counts as a template when its fixed text holds any single word character. So '%dx%d' becomes .*?x.*?, which renders every label containing an 'x', and '%s is %s' renders every label containing ' is '. probe4 found such a loose literal rendering no-id labels in test__config_rules.py ('%r validates clean') and test_gen_demo_manifest.py ('%dx%d'). End to end (probe5.py): a HEAD test file ho

The FAIL line's detail is set aside only when the label ends in ')'. A check() detail containing a newline is common: sr48 in this very test file passes text_u[-400:]. Such a detail leaves the FAIL line as 'label (first line of detail', with no closing paren. Then no literal fullmatches, so a genuinely new sentence-labelled case reads could-not-prove. probe5.py: detail 'line one\nline two' gives e

Every placeholder compiles to .*? and is fullmatched against each label form, for every string literal in both copies of the file. A literal that opens with several placeholders separated by short fixed text backtracks combinatorially. probe1.py: '%s '*6+'zq' against a 60-word label took 1.18s, and '%s '*12+'zq' did not finish in 180s. This runs after the red run and is not bounded by --timeout. O

--case now takes an id or a full label, but the Usage line still says '[--case ID ...]', the argparse help says 'a case id the task added', and the executor brief's command template says '[--case <id of the case you added>]'. An executor with a sentence-labelled case reads the template as unable to name it. Only the prose further down says 'or labels'.

_is_named now matches a pytest failure's label, which is the full nodeid. So --case tests/test_x.py::test_a narrows to that failure, and the own check (by id test_a) proves it. The refused check runs on the raw --case string instead. It finds that nodeid in neither file and adds it to refused. The proved basis then says '--case tests/test_x.py::test_a names a case HEAD's test file already carries'

The new cases pin a loose template only by a literal with no word character at all (sr54 'no fixed words'). Findings 1-3 therefore all pass the suite as it stands: a single-letter fixed literal, a multi-line detail, and a house run echoing a unittest transcript. The mutation claim ('15/15 rows red') could not have covered these shapes.

tasks.title: red-first reads a house case by its full label and the unittest reader only on unittest output
tasks.description: stamp-verification.failing_cases takes label.split()[0] as a house case's id, so a label that is a sentence starting with an ordinary word ('the', 'a') gets an id that also exists in HEAD's test file and the task's own case is never recognised; and _UNITTEST_CASE (^(FAIL|ERROR): ) is applied to every output, so a house suite whose PASSING case prints 'ERROR: <path> is not a directory' as expected stdout gets a phantom failing case. Reported on P78.9 (a new house case 'the gate-economy row is wired into diagnose() ...' read could-not-prove, exit 3, while the raw run had exactly that one FAIL line). Fix: a house case is identified by its FULL label, with a leading id-shaped token (letters then digits, e.g. me1, ga9b) used as its id only when present; the task's own case is matched by either; the unittest FAIL:/ERROR: reader applies only when the output is unittest-shaped (a 'Ran N tests' line). Cases both ways: a sentence label proves red, an id-led label is still named by its id, a house run with an expected ERROR: line counts no phantom, a real unittest ERROR: is still counted and not credited as an assertion.

tasks.title: Review findings: red-first reads only the runner that ran, and a label is judged by the most specific literal that renders it
tasks.description:
Phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (R1) failing_cases reads only the runner read_tally selected, never another runner whose tally line merely appears in the output; a case with a house run that prints a captured unittest transcript. (R2) a label is the task's own when the MOST SPECIFIC literal in the working tree that renders it (the one with the most fixed characters) is absent from HEAD's literals; a loose template such as '%dx%d' can no longer make a new case unprovable or an edited one proved; cases for both probes. (R3) a FAIL line's detail is set aside at every ' (' whether or not the line ends in ')', so a multi-line detail still matches. (R4) the label matcher is linear: the fixed parts are found in order with str.find, anchored at both ends, no regex backtracking; a case with many placeholders against a long label finishes. (R5) the Usage line, the --case help and audit-executor.md say an id or a full label. (R6) the already-carried refusal uses the same match as the proof, so a pytest nodeid is not called carried when it is not. (R7) the cases above each proven red.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:331-352 (failing_cases): Each runner is gated on its tally appearing ANYWHERE in the output. That is not the runner read_tally() chose. A house run whose passing case prints a captured unittest transcript (a 'Ran N tests' line) still gets unittest FAIL:/ERROR: phantoms, so the phase's own defect survives in that shape. The phantom FAIL: also counts as an assertion. Probe (scratchpad/p82/probe8.py): in the WT test, the existing sentence case was edited to go red, and a new passing case prints 'FAIL: test_new_rule ... Ran 3 tests ...'. `red` exit 0 proved, crediting 'test_new_rule (FAIL)' as the task's own. The only real failing case was the pre-existing one. This is a false proved. -> Read only the runner that read_tally() selects, for example failing_cases(text, runner) called with tally['runner'] from classify_run/red_verdict. Add a case: a house tally plus an echoed unittest transcript names no unittest case and does not prove.
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_pattern: A literal counts as a template when its fixed text holds any single word character. So '%dx%d' becomes .*?x.*?, which renders every label containing an 'x', and '%s is %s' renders every label containing ' is '. probe4 found such a loose literal rendering no-id labels in test__config_rules.py ('%r validates clean') and test_gen_demo_manifest.py ('%dx%d'). End to end (probe5.py): a HEAD test file holding VIEW = '%dx%d' % (1280, 720) makes a genuinely new case 'the fix sets the next value' read could-not-prove (exit 3). The same suite without that literal reads proved (exit 0). This is a false could-not-prove. In the other direction, a loose literal ADDED in WT renders an existing case that HEAD's literals fail to render. Combined with finding 3, probe6.py gives a false proved (exit 0) for an existing case whose condition was edited. The control without the literal gives exit 3. -> Judge by the most specific rendering literal, not by any literal. The case is the task's own when the literal with the most fixed text that renders the label is absent from HEAD's literal set. Alternatively, require the fixed text to anchor the label: no leading placeholder unless the fixed text holds a whole multi-letter word, and never a lone character. Add sr54 rows for '%dx%d' and '%s is %s'.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_forms: The FAIL line's detail is set aside only when the label ends in ')'. A check() detail containing a newline is common: sr48 in this very test file passes text_u[-400:]. Such a detail leaves the FAIL line as 'label (first line of detail', with no closing paren. Then no literal fullmatches, so a genuinely new sentence-labelled case reads could-not-prove. probe5.py: detail 'line one\nline two' gives exit 3 could-not-prove. The single-line control gives exit 0 proved. -> Offer the prefix before each ' (' as a form whether or not the line ends in ')', or at least when it does not. Add a case where a sentence-labelled new case has a multi-line detail.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_label_pattern / _carries_label: Every placeholder compiles to .*? and is fullmatched against each label form, for every string literal in both copies of the file. A literal that opens with several placeholders separated by short fixed text backtracks combinatorially. probe1.py: '%s '*6+'zq' against a 60-word label took 1.18s, and '%s '*12+'zq' did not finish in 180s. This runs after the red run and is not bounded by --timeout. Over the real tests/ tree it cost about 1.9s total for one long label (probe2.py), so this is latent, not observed. -> Match wildcard templates without a regex engine. Split the literal on placeholders, then check startswith(first piece), endswith(last piece) and find the middle pieces left to right. That is linear and exact for fullmatch. Or cap the placeholder count.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:39, plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:1101, plugins/audit/agents/audit-executor.md:94: --case now takes an id or a full label, but the Usage line still says '[--case ID ...]', the argparse help says 'a case id the task added', and the executor brief's command template says '[--case <id of the case you added>]'. An executor with a sentence-labelled case reads the template as unable to name it. Only the prose further down says 'or labels'. -> Say 'ID or LABEL' in all three.
R6 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py:_is_named / own_failures: _is_named now matches a pytest failure's label, which is the full nodeid. So --case tests/test_x.py::test_a narrows to that failure, and the own check (by id test_a) proves it. The refused check runs on the raw --case string instead. It finds that nodeid in neither file and adds it to refused. The proved basis then says '--case tests/test_x.py::test_a names a case HEAD's test file already carries', which is false. This is found by reading only; there is no pytest probe. -> Resolve each --case name to the failures it names, then run _added_by_task on their id/label rather than on the raw string. Alternatively, do not match pytest labels. Add a pytest nodeid --case case.
R7 (low) plugins/audit/tests/test_stamp_verification.py:_label_cases/_label_id_cases: The new cases pin a loose template only by a literal with no word character at all (sr54 'no fixed words'). Findings 1-3 therefore all pass the suite as it stands: a single-letter fixed literal, a multi-line detail, and a house run echoing a unittest transcript. The mutation claim ('15/15 rows red') could not have covered these shapes. -> Add the rows named in findings 1-3, and prove each red against the current code before the fix.
